name: Arrays & Hashing
whyNext: Foundation: counting, prefix sums and in-place tricks used everywhere later.
summary: Fundamental array and hash table patterns for fast lookups, frequency counts, and in-place manipulations.
patterns: Hash map / set for O(1) lookups and frequency counting
Prefix sum array to answer range sum queries in O(1)
In-place array indexing / sign marking for O(1) extra space
Boyer-Moore voting algorithm for majority elements

name: Two Pointers
whyNext: Uses array order; Two Sum becomes Two Sum II, then 3Sum and 4Sum.
summary: Pairwise scanning from opposite ends or at variable speeds on sorted or ordered sequences.
patterns: Inward converging pointers for sorted pair/triplet sums
Fast and slow runner pointers for in-place deduplication and partitioning
Dutch National Flag 3-pointer partition
Next permutation pivot-and-swap scan

name: Sliding Window
whyNext: Two pointers moving together over subarrays and substrings.
summary: Dynamic and fixed-size contiguous subarray and substring maintenance.
patterns: Fixed size window: add incoming, remove outgoing element
Dynamic window: expand right to satisfy condition, shrink left to minimize/restore
At-most trick: exact(K) = atMost(K) - atMost(K - 1)
Monotonic deque for sliding window maximum in O(n)

name: Binary Search
whyNext: Sorted order again, then searching on the answer itself.
summary: Halving search spaces for elements, boundaries, and monotonic answer domains.
patterns: Classic lower and upper bound binary search
Rotated sorted array: identify the sorted half and narrow range
Binary search on monotonic answer space (min max / max min capacity/days)
Staircase walk on row/column sorted 2D matrices

name: Stack
whyNext: Next greater and span ideas that later reappear in trees and DP.
summary: LIFO state tracking, matching nested structures, and monotonic stacks for nearest greater/smaller queries.
patterns: Parentheses and nested structure matching with LIFO stack
Monotonic decreasing stack for next greater element / daily temperatures
Monotonic increasing stack for largest rectangle in histogram / maximal rectangle
Greedy digit/character removal with stack

name: Linked List
whyNext: Pointer skills, reusing slow and fast pointers.
summary: Sequential node pointer manipulation, cycle detection, reversals, and reordering.
patterns: Dummy head node to simplify boundary additions/removals
Three-pointer iterative list reversal (prev, curr, next)
Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm for cycle detection and middle node
In-place interleaving and split for complex list copies

name: Backtracking
whyNext: Builds the recursion habit needed for trees and DP; ends with Target Sum, the bridge into DP.
summary: Exhaustive state space exploration, combinatorial generation, and constrained search pruning.
patterns: Subsets and combinations: choose/skip recursion with start index
Permutations: used array or swap-based backtracking
Constraint pruning: early backtrack on invalid partial states
Bridge to DP: overlapping subproblems memoization

name: Binary Trees
whyNext: Recursion on a structure; ends with House Robber III as a DP preview.
summary: Hierarchical tree traversal, depth-first search, breadth-first level orders, and structural transformations.
patterns: Bottom-up postorder DFS: solve subtrees then aggregate root result
Level order traversal using queue with level size snapshot
Path sum tracking with prefix sum hash map across ancestor paths
Tree serialization and deserialization via preorder/level order

name: Binary Search Trees
whyNext: Trees plus ordering.
summary: Exploiting the BST ordering invariant for O(h) searches, insertions, deletions, and sorted traversals.
patterns: BST search and insertion using value comparisons to prune branches
Inorder traversal produces strictly ascending sorted order
Validation using (min, max) inherited bounds
BST iterative traversal with explicit left-spine stack

name: Heap
whyNext: Kth element and streaming problems; follows sorting and BST order ideas.
summary: Min and max priority queues for top-K elements, stream medians, and greedy schedules.
patterns: Min-heap of size K for K-th largest streaming element
Two heaps (max-heap low half, min-heap high half) for running median
Multi-criteria priority queue with custom comparators
K-way merge of sorted streams / arrays

name: Greedy
whyNext: Local choices; uses sorting and heaps.
summary: Making locally optimal choices that lead to globally optimal solutions.
patterns: Sort-first greedy matching (e.g. intervals, assigning cookies)
Kadane's algorithm for maximum subarray sum
Farthest reach tracking for jump game decisions
Bidirectional / multi-pass greedy passes (e.g. candy distribution)

name: Intervals
whyNext: Sorting plus greedy sweeps.
summary: Interval overlap resolution, merges, insertions, and point-stabbing problems.
patterns: Sort by start time to linearize overlapping intervals
Sort by end time for greedy maximum non-overlapping set
Two-pointer sweep for mutual interval intersections
Difference array / sweep line for concurrency capacity counting

name: Graphs: BFS & DFS
whyNext: Trees generalised: grids, shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
summary: Connected components, grid explorations, shortest unweighted paths, and graph traversals.
patterns: Connected component flood fill via recursive DFS or iterative BFS
Multi-source BFS for simultaneous shortest distance wavefront propagation
Bipartite graph two-coloring check
Cycle detection in undirected graphs using visited sets

name: Graphs: Advanced
whyNext: Advanced graph tools on top of BFS and DFS.
summary: Directed acyclic graph ordering, disjoint set union for connectivity, and weighted shortest path algorithms.
patterns: Kahn's in-degree algorithm for DAG topological sort
Disjoint Set Union (DSU) with path compression and rank union
Dijkstra's algorithm with min-heap for non-negative weighted shortest paths
Bellman-Ford / Floyd-Warshall for edge-constrained or all-pairs shortest paths

name: DP: 1D
whyNext: Recursion with repeated work, fixed by memoisation.
summary: Subproblem optimal substructure along a single dimension with state compression.
patterns: Linear recurrence with rolling variables (Fibonacci, Climbing Stairs)
Pick vs Skip decision state transitions (House Robber)
Unbounded vs 0/1 knapsack subproblem transitions (Coin Change)
Longest increasing subsequence: O(n^2) DP and O(n log n) patience sorting

name: DP: 2D & Strings
whyNext: Grids, two-string problems, intervals and stock states.
summary: Multi-dimensional tables for grids, dual-string alignments, palindromes, and state machines.
patterns: Grid path counting and minimum cost paths (Unique Paths, Min Path Sum)
Two-string alignment matrix for LCS and Edit Distance
Interval DP: solving for all lengths from 1 to N (Burst Balloons)
Multi-state finite automata transitions (Stock trading with cooldown/fee)

name: Tries & Design
whyNext: Prefix trees and cache design, building on trees, hashing and linked lists.
summary: Prefix tree data structures for string queries and composite data structures for caching.
patterns: Trie node with 26 child pointers and isEndOfWord flag
Bitwise trie for maximum XOR pair queries
Trie combined with DFS for grid word searches
HashMap coupled with Doubly Linked List for O(1) LRU / LFU cache eviction

name: Bits & Math
whyNext: Compact tricks to finish the path.
summary: Bitwise operators, parity tricks, number theory, and prime generation algorithms.
patterns: XOR cancellation (x ^ x = 0, x ^ 0 = x) for finding unique elements
Bit clearing trick: n & (n - 1) removes lowest set bit
Bitmask representation for subset states
Sieve of Eratosthenes for prime enumeration

name: Arrays & Hashing II
whyNext: Advanced frequency counts, rolling sets, in-place signs, and coordinate hash lookups.
summary: Deepens array partitioning, prefix remainder math, and duplicate detection techniques.
patterns: Sliding window hash set / bucket indexing
Sign-inversion in-place array markers for O(1) auxiliary space
Prefix modulus frequency tracking for divisible subarrays
Two-pass running extremes for bounded sorting spans

name: Strings
whyNext: String parsing, character frequency maps, Roman numerals, and pattern matching.
summary: Character arrays, frequency arrays, big integer math, and classic KMP string matching.
patterns: 26-slot integer arrays for O(1) character frequency matching
Bidirectional mapping checks for isomorphic and pattern validation
Grade-school addition/multiplication digit-by-digit with carry
KMP prefix failure table for linear-time pattern searching

name: Two Pointers & Sliding Window II
whyNext: Advanced multi-pointer scans, variable-length windows, and greedy pairing.
summary: Refines two-pointer greedy selections, sliding subarrays with budget constraints, and dynamic window expansion.
patterns: Inward two-pointer greedy pairing for weight limits and sums
Dynamic window with at most k flips or deletions
Sliding window sum maximization with complement target matching
Prefix-sum window cost calculation for frequency equalization

name: Binary Search II
whyNext: Search on solution spaces, predicate monotonic checks, and time-based structures.
summary: Binary search on answers, mountain arrays, and parameterized feasibility functions.
patterns: Binary search on answers with monotonic feasibility verification
Upper-bound and lower-bound insertion index search
Peak slope determination in bitonic / mountain arrays
Sorted timestamp lookups for time-based key-value storage

name: Stack & Queue II
whyNext: Monotonic stacks for next smaller/greater elements, parentheses evaluation, and expression parsing.
summary: Advanced monotonic stack tracking, dual-stack simulation, and calculator parsing.
patterns: Monotonic increasing/decreasing stack for boundary finding
Dual stack design for FIFO queue emulation and arithmetic signs
Index-tracking stacks for valid parenthesis string reconstruction
Double-ended monotonic deques for sliding max/min bounds

name: Linked List & Design II
whyNext: In-place pointer rewiring, custom node structures, and O(1) data structures.
summary: Complex pointer rearrangements, dummy head sanitization, and hybrid map-array data structures.
patterns: Dummy head node for invariant deletion and partitioning
In-place segmented sublist reversals
Two-pointer gap tracking for k-th from end re-linking
HashMap combined with dynamic array for O(1) randomized retrieval

name: Backtracking II
whyNext: Pruned combinatorial search, bitmask state backtracking, and expression generation.
summary: Constraint satisfaction, grid path exploration with backtracking, and partitioned arithmetic search.
patterns: Pruned permutation tree traversal with duplicate frequency masks
Bitmask state backtracking for unique character concatenation
Grid search with in-place cell marking and restoration
Arithmetic operator insertion with running value and product tracking

name: Trees & BST II
whyNext: Advanced tree traversals, structural transformations, BST range properties, and node deletions.
summary: Decomposition of trees, subtree pruning, serialized structures, and BST invariants.
patterns: Divide and conquer subtree evaluation for node pruning and conversion
Postorder serialization for duplicate subtree detection
BST property invariants for ranged queries and node restructuring
Level-by-level BFS with node tagging and directional alternation

name: Heap, Greedy & Intervals II
whyNext: Interval scheduling, priority queues for streams, and frequency-based greedy placement.
summary: Dual heaps, greedy interval overlapping elimination, and character distance frequency queues.
patterns: Priority queue for stream tracking and multi-way element merging
Greedy interval sorting by end-times for maximum non-overlapping sets
Frequency heap with wait-queue cooldowns for string reorganization
Two-pointer interval intersection clipping

name: Matrix, Math & Bits II
whyNext: Coordinate transformations, bit manipulation arithmetic, and fast exponentiation.
summary: 2D in-place manipulations, modular arithmetic, prime sieves, and bitwise tricks.
patterns: Matrix transposition and reflection for in-place geometry transforms
Binary exponentiation by squaring in O(log n) time
Sieve of Eratosthenes for prime enumeration
Bitwise XOR and bit counting for unique element identification

name: Graphs II (BFS & DFS)
whyNext: Connected components, multi-source BFS on grids, bipartite graphs, and cycle detection.
summary: Grid flood fill, graph cloning, state-space BFS shortest path, and 2-coloring bipartite checks.
patterns: Multi-source BFS for simultaneous expansion and distance fields
Graph cloning with hash map memoization of visited nodes
2-color DFS/BFS for bipartite validation
Word transformation shortest path via bidirectional / level BFS

name: Graphs III (Topo, Union-Find, Shortest Paths)
whyNext: Topological sorting, disjoint set union with rank and path compression, and Dijkstra's algorithm.
summary: Kahn's in-degree algorithm, Union-Find connectivity, Dijkstra, and modified Bellman-Ford / BFS.
patterns: Kahn's algorithm using in-degree array for topological ordering
Disjoint Set Union (DSU) with path compression and rank optimization
Dijkstra's shortest path with min-heap priority queue
Binary search combined with BFS/DSU for min-effort path capacity

name: DP II (1D & Knapsack)
whyNext: 0/1 knapsack, unbounded knapsack, state machine DP, and subset partitioning.
summary: Optimization over value and weight budgets, state transitions, and subset sum formulations.
patterns: 0/1 Knapsack backward iteration for space optimization
Unbounded knapsack forward iteration for combinations
House robber cyclic variant with dual 1D passes
State transition arrays for sequential stock purchase and cooldown

name: DP III (2D, Strings & Intervals)
whyNext: 2D grid DP, string alignment/matching, longest common subsequence, and interval DP.
summary: Matrix traversal optimization, edit distance table transitions, and interval burst/matrix multiplication.
patterns: 2D grid path accumulation with obstacle boundary checks
Dual string alignment DP table for edit distance and wildcard matches
Longest increasing subsequence via patience sorting / binary search in O(n log n)
Interval DP scanning sub-interval lengths for optimal split points
